children.text: Released in 1954, the Rolex GMT-Master resulted from a collaboration between now-extinct airline Pan Am and Rolex on a watch that would display the time across two time zones at once. Thanks to the popularisation of commercial air travel, planes were becoming more advanced and traveling longer distances. This resulted in pilots crossing time zones during flights more frequently, and thus a need for uniformity across the aviation industry was highlighted. To eliminate errors caused by time confusion, the industry adopted a standard time-zone, Greenwich Mean Time. As such, the GMT-Master's fourth hand, its 2nd hour hand, was used to constantly display Greenwich Mean Time, as its model name implies, while its regular hour hand displayed local time. While the aviation industry's standard time-zone switched to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) in 1972, the name of the legendary GMT-Master was far too long in use for Rolex to change it. Today, the GMT-Master has become one of Rolex's most iconic models, with very few pilot's watches, if any, rivaling its level of fame, popularity, or signature design – and it certainly looks like it will stay that way.
THE BEZEL

Introduced to the GMT-Master family for the first time in its history, the ref. 126720VTNR sports a wonderfully unique green and black Cerachrom bezel - a color pairing not usually seen on GMT models.
THE CONSTRUCTION
Perhaps its most notable design detail is the ref. 126720VTNR's left-handed 'destro' design, with its winding crown found at the 9 o'clock position, alongside its date bubble.

children.text: Launched in 2023, the Rolex Yacht-Master 42 ref. 226627 is a bold and lightweight addition to Rolex’s luxury dive watch offering, the Yacht-Master collection. While the Yacht-Master was originally created as a luxurious off-shoot of the Submariner collection, it has grown to include some interesting models that break from Rolex’s typically regimented approach to dive watches. Standing as an example of that, the ref. 226627 expands the collection into a new frontier, with a grade 5 titanium case made of Rolex’s very own alloy, RLX titanium. Grey in color, incredibly light and strong, this timepiece is one of Rolex’s most visually interesting sports models yet with its black dial and matte black Cerachrom bezel retaining the collection’s roots as a sports model from Rolex. Powered by Rolex’s automatic cal. 3235 movement, the ref. 226627 boasts the same level of performance we have come to expect from The Crown, but with a new lease of life with regards to its aesthetics. Reintroducing polished lug bevels to Rolex’s ordinary production models, the ref. 226627 combines an forward-thinking approach to watchmaking with an inspired view of the past, which is the exact combination that Rolex collectors have been asking for decades, and so it is no surprise that the resulting timepiece is as popular and sought-after as it is.
THE DIAL

Boasting the same black dial design that we have come to expect from Rolex's sports models, the ref. 226627's display is admittedly familiar to Rolex collectors, with its bright white indices standing proud against their dark backdrop.
THE CONSTRUCTION

Featuring a 42mm construction made of Rolex's all-new RLX titanium, the rf. 226627's case and Oyster bracelet are incredibly lightweight and dark in color thanks to RLX's unique properties as a titanium alloy. Additionally, Rolex has finally reintroduced polished bevels to the lugs of their watches, albeit only available on their Titanum models.

children.text: A legendary timepiece with an unrivaled history, the Rolex Day-Date has earned its place as "The Ultimate Watch of Prestige" from its decades on the wrists of the world's most influential people. Released in 1956, the Day-Date quickly became synonymous with luxury, prestige, and exclusivity thanks to being the watch of choice for the world's athletes, visionaries, and world leaders alike. Only ever constructed of precious metals, the Day-Date's aesthetic is that of sheer elegance and grace. Aside from the beautiful array of dial options that have been available over the decades, the Day-Date's most iconic piece of design is its three-piece "Presidential" or "President" bracelet. Forming the bedrock of its design, the Presidential bracelet has become synonymous with Rolex's flagship collection and their desire to create the very best and most iconic watches that the world has ever seen. With its timeless design and inescapable impact on horology, the Day-Date stands as a vivid reminder of just how successful they have been in realizing that very mission.

children.text: Released to celebrate Rolex's 40th anniversary in 1945, the Rolex Datejust has become one of the Genevan Giant's most iconic watches. The world's first wristwatch to display the date via an aperture on the dial, the Datejust revolutionized wristwatch design for decades to follow. With its emblematic Cyclops lens, jubilee bracelet (designed specifically for the model in 1945), and classy fluted precious metal bezel, the Datejust's aesthetic has always been that of pure elegance and class. Perhaps one of Rolex's most recognizable designs, the Datejust has evolved from its dressier roots into a perfectly capable timepiece rivaling the robustness of most brand's sports watches. Featuring a stainless steel case with a screw-down crown and caseback, the Datejust packs an impressive 100m of water resistance alongside its consistently capable movements and construction that have enabled it to become one of the best-equipped watches for daily wear and tear. Available with several different dial options, in a multitude of materials, and across many styles, the Datejust is an inescapable reflection of its owner, with a model out there to suit pretty much everybody's tastes and preferences.

Boasting a stunning silver diamond-set dial with a subtle golden undertone, this ref. 278278 features a gentle monochromatic aesthetic that is perfectly complemented by its diamond-set hour markers.

children.text: Debuting in 1953 and released to the public the following year, the Rolex Submariner has undoubtedly become one of the most iconic timepieces of all time thanks to its legendary status as Rolex's flagship dive watch. Used extensively by the British Royal Navy and professional diving operations like COMEX, the Submariner set the bar for all dive watches to follow. Featuring a genuinely timeless design that has remained relatively unchanged throughout its history, this Rolex has become the archetypal sports watch. With very few large-scale aesthetic upgrades made to it over the years except for timely advancements like introducing a date function to the collection in the late '60s, and its modern cerachrom bezels, the Submariner is seen as the prototypical dive watch thanks to its consistency. The Submariner has earned its status as a legendary watch, with it today remaining as one of the most sought-after timepieces around.

Launched in 1958 as one of many Submariner references that were introduced in the late 1950s as Rolex tried to balance the collection’s legibility and durabilty with its performance and looks, the Submariner ref. 5508 is a famed reference amongst collectors for a host of reasons. Famed as the last 38mm Submariner reference, the ref. 5508 features purest essence of the Submariner’s vintage spirit, which is also communicated through its lack of crown guards and accompanying small crown, which was only 6mm – 2mm smaller than crowns on previous and subsequent Submariner references. Additionally, given the evolving demands of dive watches at the time, the ref. 5508 was the last Submariner reference to be water resistance to 100m. A truly iconic model that has its place with the Submariner’s history the ref. 5508 holds its own with so many of its iconic siblings and so we are delighted to have one with us here at Loupe This.
THE DIAL

Sporting golden gilt inscriptions atop its deep black backdrop and beautifully aged luminous tritium plots and hands, this ref. 5508 example boasts a beautifully preserved service dial that is just stunning.
THE CONSTRUCTION

Iconic in its styling and design, the Submariner 5508's beautiful 38mm stainless steel construction fits the wrist perfectly today just as it did back when it was launched. With its small crown and lack of crown guards, it is unique on the wrist and brings that vintage flavor that collectors cherish so much.

The bezel is well defined, and the later black insert is very clean with a tight crack visible in the "triangle". The SWISS T 25 dial shows light surface aging, with luminous that has aged to a pleasing dark tone.  The tone of luminous is slightly darker in the lower left quadrant.  Hands have a luminous shade similar in tone with some cracks and discolorations.  The Swiss rivet bracelet has been repaired at some point and the clasp comes from a later Jubilee bracelet. The bracelet has 10 links and fits an approximately 6 3/4” wrist.  It shows light stretch.

With its unique design details like its small crown, gilt dial, lack of crown guards and 38mm case, the ref. 5508 is a wonderful Submariner to wear that is rich in heritage and the Submariner's iconic design.

children.text: Introduced in 1955, the Rolex Submariner reference 6538 is one of the most celebrated sports watches ever produced. Building on the success of the earliest Submariner references, it introduced the now-famous oversized 8mm winding crown, earning the enduring nickname "Big Crown." Produced for only a few years before the arrival of crown guards on the reference 5512, the 6538 represents the purest expression of Rolex's original professional dive watch, combining uncompromising functionality with proportions that have become legendary among collectors.
The reference's place in popular culture was cemented when Sean Connery wore a 6538 in
Dr. No

(1962), marking the first appearance of a Rolex on James Bond's wrist. That association transformed an already important dive watch into one of the most recognisable wristwatches ever made. This particular example has been sympathetically maintained with Rolex service dial and hands, preserving its practicality while remaining unmistakably a 6538. Fitted to the quintessential single-pass nylon strap associated with Bond's early appearances on screen, it captures the spirit of one of cinema's most iconic watches while remaining one of the defining references in Rolex's sporting history.
THE DIAL

This example is fitted with a Rolex service gloss black dial and hands, with tritium lume instead of the original radium. This iconic dial layout provides outstanding legibility combined with the unmistakable character of the Rolex Submariner.
THE CONSTRUCTION

The 6538's defining feature is its oversized 8mm winding crown, fitted without crown guards for maximum ease of operation underwater. Combined with the slim case and beautifully bevelled lugs, it creates one of the most recognisable silhouettes in vintage watchmaking.
TIMING MACHINE READOUT

This reading was taken (crown down) with a ONEOF Accuracy Boutique Edition timing machine at time of cataloging. It is provided as a courtesy only, and shall not be construed as a warranty or guarantee of any kind. Please refer to our terms and conditions of sale for more information.

Watch is in overall excellent condition. The steel case shows surface scratches and light nicks, as expected of a tool watch of this vintage. The steel Rolex service bezel remains well defined, whilst the
aftermarket

"Crown Art Customs" red triangle insert has a few small marks. The 8mm Brevet winding crown shows significant wear. The tritium service dial and hands are in near-mint condition. The serial number- 126314, is present but is partially worn out and only fully visible with a loupe. It is fitted with a fabric strap.
Please note:
The watch ticks at the time of cataloging, but timekeeping is poor and a service is recommended.

Few vintage Rolex references command the admiration of the 6538. Revered by collectors for its oversized crown, short production run and enduring connection to James Bond, it occupies a unique position within the history of the Submariner. While fitted with Rolex service components, this remains an immensely charismatic example of one of the most iconic sports watches ever produced.
